topic: When plans fall apart outside our control: rain on a run day, the gym closed, the day rearranged; fighting what already happened changes nothing, so we accept it willingly and adjust the session instead of sulking or skipping
figure: Cleanthes of Assos, second head of the Stoic school after Zeno, c. 330-230 BC (his verses quoted by Epictetus, Enchiridion 53, and translated by Seneca, Moral Letters 107.11: lead me, Zeus and Destiny, and I will follow without hesitation; if I am unwilling I will follow all the same; Seneca adds: the fates lead the willing and drag the unwilling). Paraphrased, not quoted. Single quote page, at Mintra's request

lines: ฝนตก ยิมปิด แผนพัง
เราเลือกไม่ได้
แต่เลือกได้ว่าจะไปต่อ
แบบฝืนใจ หรือเต็มใจ
